name: dn-empty-permitted-subtree-valid
description: A permittedSubtrees directoryName whose DN has zero RDNs (the X.500 root) admits any non-empty subject DN as a subordinate, since the empty sequence is a prefix of every sequence. RFC 5280 6.1.4 even calls this case out explicitly: 'if a name of the relevant type in a permitted subtree is empty (zero attributes), then the subtree is the entire name space of that type.' A leaf with an unrelated subject must therefore be accepted.
notes: Implemented by injecting the nameConstraints extension via the unknown_extensions DER escape hatch because cryptography refuses to emit an empty SEQUENCE OF for the constraint name. The DER is the equivalent of an extnValue containing a sequence with permittedSubtrees [0] { GeneralSubtree { directoryName [4] EXPLICIT { SEQUENCE OF RDN { } } } }.

Observed behaviour across the corpus's validators: all five reject. OpenSSL and Go bail out at parse time ('invalid certificate' / 'invalid NameConstraints extension'); Botan reports an extension encoding error; Rust treats the encoding as BadDer; GnuTLS reports a constraint violation. So while RFC 5280 6.1.4 makes this a 'permits everything' constraint, no surveyed implementation honours it — that's the finding.
